text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet Thursday bowed to growing protests against the new social insurance rules that took effect early this year, and agreed to urgently submit new, retroactive regulations to Parliament next week.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said Hungary greatly appreciates the progress made in many areas of bilateral relations with Slovakia, but cannot ignore matters affecting the assertion of minority rights.
- The central budget incurred a surplus of HUF 15.7 billion in January, Finance Ministry deputy state secretary Csaba Laszlo announced yesterday.
- Grape growers will carry out their threat to block roads in the southern and eastern counties of Bacs-Kiskun, Szolnok and Csongrad today.
- The mobile phone company Pannon GSM will launch Hungary's largest corporate bond issue to date on February 20, announced managing director Emri Gussi.
- The 1996 after-tax profit of Graboplast and its subsidiaries exceeded HUF 1.4 billion, nearly 200 percent above the 1995 figure.

- The Budapest electricity works Elmu made a HUF 3.5 billion loss last year and only hopes to break even in 1997, despite the 24.9 percent rise in electricity prices in January, company president Emmerich Endresz announced.
- Police have charged former Hungarian swimming team manager Gyorgy Zemplenyi with 31 counts of fraud and four counts of embezzlement causing damages in excess of HUF 452 million.
NEPSZABADSAG

- A large number of forged HUF 5,000 banknotes are in circulation, in part because Hungarian police groups failed to track the illegal shipment of high-quality German paper used in the forgeries, despite an advance tip-off from German authorities.
- The parliamentary commission probing the Tocsik affair will hear Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Free Democrat president Ivan Peto on Monday.
- Hungary's largest trade union federations will hold a closed-door summit today and Saturday in Balatonszemes, their first such gathering since the change of regime.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Some HUF 1,200 billion, at current prices, was invested in the national economy last year.
- The east Hungary electricity company Titasz piled up a loss of HUF 2.1 billion in 1996.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- About 100,000 tonnes of potatoes stored in Hungary may be left to rot because of last year's overabundant harvest of 1.2 million tonnes, the Potato Product Council predicts.
- Primagaz yesterday reported a HUF 2 billion pre-tax profit for 1996.
- The 1996 pre-tax profit of the pharmaceutical company Human came to HUF 712 million exceeding last year's figure by 44 percent.
- The 1996 pre-tax profit of Corvinbank came to HUF 10 million, 40 percent less than in 1995. Konzumbank's 1996 pre-tax profit quadrupled to HUF 95 million over the previous year's figure.
- The country's 19 state-owned forestry companies generated a collective HUF 1 billion pre-tax profit on revenues of HUF 27.7 billion last year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
